Evaluate one prepared subject

Source: R/subjects.R
pmx_ode_subject_eval.Rd

One subject's predictions and residual variances at its observation records, at theta and eta: what an estimator needs to form the likelihood. The predictions are the doubles pmx_ode_solve() gives for the same subject and parameters. This is zupmxode_subject_eval() of the C API (inst/include/zupmxode.h), one R call per subject.

Usage

pmx_ode_subject_eval(
  model,
  subject,
  theta = double(),
  eta = double(),
  sigma,
  tol = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A model from pmx_ode_model().

subject

One element of pmx_ode_subjects()'s result.

theta, eta

Named numeric vectors with the parameters the subject was prepared with (attr(subjects, "theta") and attr(subjects, "eta")), in any order.

sigma

The output and its error model, a list of one element, as in pmx_ode_sim(): list(cp = prop(0.1)).

tol

The general solvers' tolerances, c(rtol, atol); NULL for the model's.

Value

A list with time, pred and var, one value each per observation record.

Details

The variance follows the error model, f the prediction: add(a) gives a^2, prop(b) gives (b * f)^2, add(a) + prop(b) their sum, and lnorm(s) gives s^2, the variance on the log scale.

Errors

pmx_ode_error_argument for arguments that do not match the subject and model, or a subject saved and loaded again; pmx_ode_error_events and pmx_ode_error_solver as for pmx_ode_solve().

Warnings

pmx_ode_warning_solver when the solver fails: pred and var are NA from there. pmx_ode_warning_steady_state when a steady state does not converge.

Examples

m <- pmx_ode_model({
  cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl); v <- exp(tv); ka <- exp(tka)
  cp <- linCmt()
})
ev <- pmx_ode_events(amt = 100, cmt = "depot", time = c(1, 4, 12, 24))
subs <- pmx_ode_subjects(m, ev)
attr(subs, "theta")
#> [1] "tcl" "tv"  "tka"
pmx_ode_subject_eval(m, subs[[1]], theta = c(tcl = 0, tv = 3, tka = -0.5),
                     eta = c(eta.cl = 0.1), sigma = list(cp = prop(0.1)))
#> $time
#> [1]  1  4 12 24
#> 
#> $pred
#> [1] 2.196872 3.909813 2.825413 1.461862
#> 
#> $var
#> [1] 0.04826248 0.15286634 0.07982960 0.02137041
#>
